Reasoning

法院生效裁判认为，最高人民法院《关于审理侵犯专利权纠纷案件应用法律若干问题的解释》第七条规定：“人民法院判定被诉侵权技术方案是否落入专利权的保护范围，应当审查权利人主张的权利要求所记载的全部技术特征。被诉侵权技术方案包含与权利要求记载的全部技术特征相同或者等同的技术特征的，人民法院应当认定其落入专利权的保护范围；被诉侵权技术方案的技术特征与权利要求记载的全部技术特征相比，缺少权利要求记载的一个以上的技术特征，或者有一个以上技术特征不相同也不等同的，人民法院应当认定其没有落入专利权的保护范围。”本案中，华生公司被诉生产销售的药品与涉案专利方法制备的产品相同，均为奥氮平，判定华生公司奥氮平制备工艺是否落入涉案专利权保护范围，涉及以下三个问题：

The effective judgment of the court held that Article 7 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases provides: "When a people's court determines whether the accused infringing technical solution falls within the scope of protection of a patent right, it shall examine all the technical features described in the claim asserted by the right holder. If the accused infringing technical solution contains technical features that are identical or equivalent to all the technical features described in the claim, the people's court shall determine that it falls within the scope of protection of the patent right; if, compared with all the technical features described in the claim, the technical features of the accused infringing technical solution lack one or more technical features described in the claim, or have one or more technical features that are neither identical nor equivalent, the people's court shall determine that it does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent right." In this case, the drug that Huasheng Company was accused of producing and selling is the same as the product prepared by the patented method in suit, both being olanzapine. Determining whether Huasheng Company's olanzapine preparation process falls within the scope of protection of the patent in suit involves the following three issues:

（一）关于涉案专利权的保护范围

(1) Concerning the scope of protection of the patent in suit

专利法第五十六条第一款规定：“发明或者实用新型专利权的保护范围以其权利要求的内容为准，说明书及附图可以用于解释权利要求。”本案中，礼来公司要求保护涉案专利权利要求1中的方法（a），该权利要求采取开放式的撰写方式，其中仅限定了参加取代反应的三环还原物及N-甲基哌嗪以及发生取代的基团，其保护范围涵盖了所有采用所述三环还原物与N-甲基哌嗪在Q基团处发生取代反应而生成奥氮平的制备方法，无论采用何种反应起始物、溶剂、反应条件，均在其保护范围之内。基于此，判定华生公司奥氮平制备工艺是否落入涉案专利权保护范围，关键在于两个技术方案反应路线的比对，而具体的反应起始物、溶剂、反应条件等均不纳入侵权比对范围，否则会不当限缩涉案专利权的保护范围，损害礼来公司的合法权益。

Article 56(1) of the Patent Law provides: "The scope of protection of an invention or utility model patent right shall be determined by the content of its claims. The description and drawings may be used to interpret the claims." In this case, Lilly Company requested protection for method (a) in claim 1 of the patent in suit. This claim is drafted in an open-ended format, and only defines the tricyclic reduced compound and N-methylpiperazine participating in the substitution reaction, as well as the substituting group. Its scope of protection covers all preparation methods that generate olanzapine through the substitution reaction between the tricyclic reduced compound and N-methylpiperazine at the Q group, regardless of the specific reaction starting materials, solvents, or reaction conditions used, all of which fall within its scope of protection. Based on this, the key to determining whether Huasheng Company's olanzapine preparation process falls within the scope of protection of the patent in suit lies in a comparison of the reaction routes of the two technical solutions. The specific reaction starting materials, solvents, reaction conditions, etc., are not included in the scope of the infringement comparison; otherwise, the scope of protection of the patent in suit would be improperly limited, harming Lilly Company's legitimate rights and interests.

（二）关于华生公司实际使用的奥氮平制备工艺

(2) Concerning the olanzapine preparation process actually used by Huasheng Company

专利法第五十七条第二款规定：“专利侵权纠纷涉及新产品制造方法的发明专利的，制造同样产品的单位或者个人应当提供其产品制造方法不同于专利方法的证明。”本案中，双方当事人对奥氮平为专利法中所称的新产品不持异议，华生公司应就其奥氮平制备工艺不同于涉案专利方法承担举证责任。具体而言，华生公司应当提供证据证明其实际使用的奥氮平制备工艺反应路线未落入涉案专利权保护范围，否则，将因其举证不能而承担推定礼来公司侵权指控成立的法律后果。

Article 57(2) of the Patent Law provides: "Where a patent infringement dispute involves a patent for a method for manufacturing a new product, the entity or individual manufacturing the same product shall provide proof that its method for manufacturing the product is different from the patented method." In this case, both parties do not dispute that olanzapine is a new product within the meaning of the Patent Law. Huasheng Company bears the burden of proving that its olanzapine preparation process is different from the patented method in suit. Specifically, Huasheng Company shall provide evidence to prove that the reaction route of the olanzapine preparation process it actually uses does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent in suit; otherwise, due to its failure to meet the burden of proof, it shall bear the legal consequence of the presumption that Lilly Company's infringement allegations are established.

本案中，华生公司主张其自2003年至今一直使用2008年向国家药监局补充备案工艺生产奥氮平，并提交了其2003年和2008年奥氮平批生产记录（一审补充证据6）、2003年、2007年和2013年生产规程（一审补充证据7）、《药品补充申请批件》（一审补充证据12）等证据证明其实际使用的奥氮平制备工艺。如前所述，本案的侵权判定关键在于两个技术方案反应路线的比对，华生公司2008年补充备案工艺的反应路线可见于其向国家药监局提交的《奥氮平药品补充申请注册资料》，其中5.1“原料药生产工艺的研究资料及文献资料”之5.1.2“工艺路线”图显示该反应路线为：先将“仲胺化物”中的仲氨基用苄基保护起来，制得“苄基化物”（苄基化），再进行闭环反应，生成“苄基取代的噻吩并苯并二氮杂”三环化合物（还原化物）。“还原化物”中的氨基被N-甲基哌嗪取代，生成“缩合物”，然后脱去苄基，制得奥氮平。本院认为，现有在案证据能够形成完整证据链，证明华生公司2003年至涉案专利权到期日期间一直使用其2008年补充备案工艺的反应路线生产奥氮平，主要理由如下：

In this case, Huasheng Company claimed that it had been producing olanzapine using the process filed in its 2008 supplementary application with the SDA from 2003 to the present, and submitted its 2003 and 2008 olanzapine batch production records (first-instance supplementary evidence 6), 2003, 2007, and 2013 production procedures (first-instance supplementary evidence 7), the "Drug Supplementary Application Approval" (first-instance supplementary evidence 12), and other evidence to prove its actually used olanzapine preparation process. As previously stated, the key to determining infringement in this case lies in comparing the reaction routes of the two technical solutions. The reaction route of Huasheng Company's 2008 supplementary filed process can be seen in the "Olanzapine Drug Supplementary Application Registration Materials" it submitted to the SDA. Section 5.1.2 "Process Route" under Section 5.1 "Research Materials and Literature on the API Production Process" showed that the reaction route is: first, protect the secondary amino group in the "secondary amine compound" with a benzyl group to produce a "benzylated compound" (benzylation), then conduct a ring-closing reaction to generate a "benzyl-substituted thienobenzodiazepine" tricyclic compound (the reduced compound). The amino group in the "reduced compound" is substituted by N-methylpiperazine to generate a "condensation compound," and then debenzylation occurs to produce olanzapine. This Court holds that the existing evidence in the case can form a complete chain of evidence proving that Huasheng Company had been using the reaction route of its 2008 supplementary filed process to produce olanzapine from 2003 until the expiration of the patent in suit. The main reasons are as follows:

首先，华生公司2008年向国家药监局提出奥氮平药品补充申请注册，在其提交的《奥氮平药品补充申请注册资料》中，明确记载了其奥氮平制备工艺的反应路线。针对该补充申请，江苏省药监部门于2009年7月7日和8月25日对华生公司进行了生产现场检查和产品抽样，并出具了《药品注册生产现场检查报告》（受理号CXHB0800159），该报告显示华生公司的“生产过程按申报的工艺进行”，三批样品“已按抽样要求进行了抽样”，现场检查结论为“通过”。也就是说，华生公司2008年补充备案工艺经过药监部门的现场检查，具备可行性。基于此，2010年9月8日，国家药监局向华生公司颁发了《药品补充申请批件》，同意华生公司奥氮平“变更生产工艺并修订质量标准”。对于华生公司2008年补充备案工艺的可行性，礼来公司专家辅助人在二审庭审中予以认可，江苏省科技咨询中心出具的（2014）司鉴字第02号《技术鉴定报告》在其鉴定结论部分也认为“华生公司2008年向国家药监局备案的奥氮平制备工艺是可行的”。因此，在无其他相反证据的情形下，应当推定华生公司2008年补充备案工艺即为其取得《药品补充申请批件》后实际使用的奥氮平制备工艺。

First, in 2008, Huasheng Company filed a supplementary application for registration of the olanzapine drug with the SDA. In the submitted "Olanzapine Drug Supplementary Application Registration Materials," the reaction route of its olanzapine preparation process was clearly recorded. In response to this supplementary application, the Jiangsu drug regulatory authorities conducted an on-site production inspection and product sampling of Huasheng Company on July 7 and August 25, 2009, and issued a "Drug Registration Production Site Inspection Report" (Acceptance No. CXHB0800159). The report showed that Huasheng Company's "production process was carried out according to the declared process," the three batches of samples "had been sampled as required," and the on-site inspection conclusion was "Passed." That is to say, Huasheng Company's 2008 supplementary filed process had passed the on-site inspection by the drug regulatory authorities and was feasible. Based on this, on September 8, 2010, the SDA issued a "Drug Supplementary Application Approval" to Huasheng Company, approving Huasheng Company's olanzapine to "change the production process and revise the quality standards." Regarding the feasibility of Huasheng Company's 2008 supplementary filed process, Lilly Company's technical assistant expert acknowledged it during the second-instance trial. The Technical Appraisal Report No. (2014) Si Jian Zi 02 issued by the Jiangsu Science and Technology Consulting Center also concluded in its appraisal conclusion that "the olanzapine preparation process filed by Huasheng Company with the SDA in 2008 is feasible." Therefore, in the absence of other contrary evidence, it should be presumed that Huasheng Company's 2008 supplementary filed process is the olanzapine preparation process it actually used after obtaining the "Drug Supplementary Application Approval."

其次，一般而言，适用于大规模工业化生产的药品制备工艺步骤繁琐，操作复杂，其形成不可能是一蹴而就的。从研发阶段到实际生产阶段，其长期的技术积累过程通常是在保持基本反应路线稳定的情况下，针对实际生产中发现的缺陷不断优化调整反应条件和操作细节。华生公司的奥氮平制备工艺受让于医科院药物所，双方于1999年10月28日签订了《技术转让合同》。按照合同约定，医科院药物所负责完成临床前报批资料并在北京申报临床。在医科院药物所1999年10月填报的（京99）药申临字第82号《新药临床研究申请表》中，“制备工艺”栏绘制的反应路线显示，其采用了与华生公司2008年补充备案工艺相同的反应路线。针对该新药临床研究申请，北京市卫生局1999年11月9日作出《新药研制现场考核报告表》，确认“原始记录、实验资料基本完整，内容真实。”在此基础上，医科院药物所和华生公司按照《技术转让合同》的约定，共同向国家药监局提交新药证书、生产申请表（（2001）京申产字第019号）。针对该申请，江苏省药监局2001年10月22日作出《新药研制现场考核报告表》，确认“样品制备及检验原始记录基本完整”。通过包括前述考核在内的一系列审查后，2003年5月9日，医科院药物所和华生公司获得国家药监局颁发的奥氮平原料药和奥氮平片《新药证书》。由此可见，华生公司自1999年即拥有了与其2008年补充备案工艺反应路线相同的奥氮平制备工艺，并以此申报新药注册，取得新药证书。因此，华生公司在2008补充备案工艺之前使用反应路线完全不同的其他制备工艺生产奥氮平的可能性不大。

Second, generally speaking, drug preparation processes suitable for large-scale industrial production are cumbersome with complex operations, and their formation cannot be achieved overnight. From the research and development stage to the actual production stage, the long-term technical accumulation process usually involves continuously optimizing and adjusting reaction conditions and operational details to address defects discovered in actual production while maintaining a stable basic reaction route. Huasheng Company's olanzapine preparation process was transferred from the IMM, CAMS, and the parties entered into a "Technology Contract" on October 28, 1999. According to the contract, the IMM, CAMS was responsible for completing the pre-clinical submission materials and filing the clinical application in Beijing. The reaction route depicted in the "Preparation Process" column of the "Application Form for New Drug Clinical Research" No. (Jing 99) Yao Shen Lin Zi 82, completed by the IMM, CAMS in October 1999, showed that it used the same reaction route as Huasheng Company's 2008 supplementary filed process. In response to this new drug clinical research application, the Beijing Municipal Health Bureau issued a "Report Form for On-Site Inspection of New Drug Development" on November 9, 1999, confirming that "the original records and experimental materials are basically complete and the content is authentic." On this basis, the IMM, CAMS and Huasheng Company, in accordance with the Technology Contract, jointly submitted the "Application Form for New Drug Certificate and Production" (No. (2001) Jing Shen Chan Zi 019) to the SDA. In response to this application, the Jiangsu Provincial Drug Administration issued a "Report Form for On-Site Inspection of New Drug Development" on October 22, 2001, confirming that "the original records of sample preparation and testing are basically complete." After a series of reviews including the aforementioned inspections, on May 9, 2003, the IMM, CAMS and Huasheng Company obtained the "New Drug Certificates" for olanzapine API and olanzapine tablets issued by the SDA. Thus, it can be seen that Huasheng Company has possessed the olanzapine preparation process with the same reaction route as its 2008 supplementary filed process since 1999, and used it to apply for new drug registration and obtain the new drug certificate. Therefore, it is unlikely that Huasheng Company used a completely different reaction route for the production of olanzapine before its 2008 supplementary filed process.

Finally, the "Approval Conclusion" column of the Drug Supplementary Application Approval issued by the National Medical Products Administration to Huasheng Company on September 8, 2010, recorded: "The changed production process, while not altering the original synthetic route, only adjusts the solvents and reagents used in the preparation process." That is, the National Medical Products Administration confirmed that the 2008 supplementary filing process of Huasheng Company had the same reaction route as its previous preparation process. Huasheng Company submitted its 2003, 2007, and 2013 production procedures, and the 2003 and 2008 batch production records for olanzapine in the first instance. Huasheng Company claimed that the above evidence involved its trade secrets, and the court at first instance organized an in camera cross-examination for both parties, confirming its authenticity and relevance. This court finds upon review that the 2003 and 2008 batch production records for olanzapine by Huasheng Company were records of actual production based on the 2003 and 2007 production procedures, respectively. The above production procedures and batch production records both show that the basic reaction route of Huasheng Company's olanzapine preparation process is the same as the reaction route of its 2008 supplementary filing process, with only adjustments to production details such as reaction conditions and solvents while maintaining the basic reaction route, and continuous optimization. Such a process of technical accumulation is consistent with actual production laws.

In summary, this court holds that Huasheng Company's 2008 supplementary filing process is true and feasible, and from 2003 to the expiration date of the patent in question, Huasheng Company has consistently used the reaction route of the 2008 supplementary filing process to produce olanzapine.

(III) Whether Eli Lilly's infringement allegations are established

Comparing the reaction route of Huasheng Company's olanzapine preparation process with the method patent in question, the differences lie in the different reaction steps and different key intermediates. Specifically, in Huasheng Company's olanzapine preparation process, the amino group of the tricyclic reduction product is benzyl-protected, so there must necessarily be a benzylation reaction step before the substitution reaction to generate the benzylated tricyclic reduction product, and correspondingly, a debenzylation reaction step after the substitution reaction to obtain olanzapine. However, in the reaction route of the patent in question, the amino group of the tricyclic reduction product is not benzyl-protected, so there are no corresponding benzylation and debenzylation reaction steps.

Article 17, Paragraph 2 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Dispute Cases stipulates: "Equivalent features refer to features that realize substantially the same function, achieve substantially the same effect, and are features that a person of ordinary skill in the art can conceive of without creative labor at the time of the alleged infringement, using substantially the same means as the described technical features." In this case, regarding the differences between the reaction route of Huasheng Company's olanzapine preparation process and the method patent in question: First, the benzyl-protected tricyclic reduction product intermediate and the non-benzyl-protected tricyclic reduction product intermediate are different compounds, with different chemical reaction characteristics. Specifically, on the non-benzyl-protected tricyclic reduction product intermediate, both the detachable Q group and the amino group can react with N-methylpiperazine, while on the benzyl-protected tricyclic reduction product intermediate, since the amino group is benzyl-protected, it cannot undergo an undesired substitution reaction with N-methylpiperazine, and the substitution reaction can only occur at the Q group. Correspondingly, in the method of the patent in question, there are no benzylation and debenzylation reaction steps before and after the substitution reaction. Therefore, there are significant differences between the two technical solutions in terms of reaction intermediates and reaction steps. Second, because of the addition of benzylation and debenzylation steps, Huasheng Company's olanzapine preparation process suffers a reduction in the yield of the final product, whereas the patent in question does not suffer a reduction in yield due to the absence of those steps. Therefore, there are significant differences in technical effects, such as yield, between the two technical solutions. Finally, although benzyl-protecting the amino group in the tricyclic reduction product to reduce side reactions is common general knowledge in the field of chemical synthesis, this change is substantial. The reaction characteristics of the benzyl-protected tricyclic reduction product intermediate have changed, and the addition of reaction steps also reduces the yield. Moreover, that benzyl protection is common general knowledge only indicates that Huasheng Company's olanzapine preparation process has limited improvement over the method patent in question, but does not mean that the technical means employed by the two are substantially the same.

In summary, Huasheng Company's olanzapine preparation process differs from the method patent in question in terms of whether the tricyclic reduction product intermediate is a benzylated intermediate and the resulting addition of benzylation and debenzylation reaction steps. The corresponding technical features do not constitute substantially the same technical means, and the technical effects achieved are significantly different; thus, they do not constitute equivalent features. Therefore, Huasheng Company's olanzapine preparation process does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent in question.

In conclusion, Huasheng Company's olanzapine preparation process does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent in question owned by Eli Lilly. The first-instance judgment had errors in the determination of facts and application of law, and is hereby corrected in accordance with the law.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Zhou Xiang, Wu Rong, Song Shuhua)

Guiding Case No. 85

Grohe AG v. Zhejiang Jianlong Sanitary Ware Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of design patent

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, published on March 6, 2017)

Keywords: civil; infringement of design patent; design features; functional features; overall visual effect

Ruling Gist

1. The design features of the granted design embody its innovative content different from the prior design and also reflect the designer's creative contribution to the prior design. If the alleged infringing design does not include all the design features that distinguish the granted design from the prior design, it can generally be presumed that the alleged infringing design is not similar to the granted design.

2. The determination of design features shall be made by the patentee providing evidence for the design features it claims. On the basis of hearing the cross-examination opinions of all parties, the people's court shall fully review the evidence and determine the design features of the granted design in accordance with the law.

3. The determination of functional design features depends on whether, from the perspective of the ordinary consumer of the design patent product, the design is solely determined by a specific function, without considering whether the design possesses aesthetic appeal. Functional design features do not have a significant impact on the overall visual effect of the design. Design features that are both functional and ornamental have an impact on the overall visual effect that depends on the strength of the ornamental aspect. The stronger the ornamental aspect, the greater the impact on the overall visual effect, and vice versa.

Related Legal Provisions

Article 59, Paragraph 2 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

Grohe AG (hereinafter referred to as Grohe) is the patentee of the design patent for "Handheld Shower Head (No. A4284410X2)," which is currently valid and in force. In November 2012, Grohe filed a lawsuit against Zhejiang Jianlong Sanitary Ware Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jianlong), alleging that Jianlong's production, sale, and offer for sale of the Liya series and other sanitary ware products infringed its design patent for the "Handheld Shower Head." Grohe requested the court to order Jianlong to immediately cease the alleged infringing acts, destroy the inventory of infringing products and molds specially used for producing the infringing products, and compensate Grohe for economic losses of RMB 200,000. After a comparison at the first-instance trial, the similarities between Jianlong's alleged infringing product and Grohe's design patent in question were as follows: both products were of the same type; overall, both consisted of a head portion and a handle portion; the shape of the water outlet surface of the head of the alleged infringing product was the same as that of the patent in question, both showing a pattern of outlet holes distributed radially within an area that is rounded at both ends and rectangular in the middle, with curved edges. The differences between the two were: 1. The four sides of the head of the alleged infringing product were sloped, tilting from the back toward the water outlet, while the front view and left view of the patent in question showed the four sides of the head as curved surfaces; 2. On the head of the alleged infringing product, the water outlet surface was separated from the panel by a single line, while on the patent in question, the water outlet surface was separated from the panel by a band formed by two lines; 3. The distribution of outlet holes on the water outlet surface of the head of the alleged infringing product was slightly different from that of the patent in question; 4. The handle of the patent in question had an oval switch design, which the alleged infringing product did not have; 5. Although the connection between the head and the handle in the patent in question had a certain angled slant, the angle was very small, almost a straight-line connection, while the connection between the head and the handle of the alleged infringing product had a larger angled slant; 6. From the bottom view of the patent in question, the bottom of the handle was circular, while the bottom of the alleged infringing product in the bottom view was a curved fan shape; the lower part of the handle of the patent in question was cylindrical, gradually contracting and flattening into a flat elliptical shape toward the connection area with the head, while the lower part of the handle of the alleged infringing product was a fan-shaped column, and the transition to the connection with the head was entirely a fan-shaped column, with a curved protrusion in the middle section of the handle during the transition; 7. There was a curved decorative line at the bottom end of the handle of the alleged infringing product, connecting the bottom end of the handle with the back of the product, while the patent in question had no such design at the bottom end of the handle; 8. The length ratio of the head to the handle of the patent in question differed from that of the alleged infringing product, and the curved surface at the connection between the head and the handle also differed.

Judgment

The Taizhou Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province rendered the civil judgment (2012) Zhe Tai Zhi Min Chu Zi No. 573 on March 5, 2013, dismissing the claims of Grohe AG. Grohe AG appealed. The Zhejiang High People's Court rendered the civil judgment (2013) Zhe Zhi Zhong Zi No. 255 on September 27, 2013: 1. Reversing the civil judgment (2012) Zhe Tai Zhi Min Chu Zi No. 573 of the Taizhou Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province; 2. Ordering Zhejiang Jianlong Sanitary Ware Co., Ltd. to immediately cease manufacturing, offering for sale, and selling products that infringe the design patent for "Handheld Shower Head" owned by Grohe AG, and to destroy the inventory of infringing products; 3. Ordering Zhejiang Jianlong Sanitary Ware Co., Ltd. to compensate Grohe AG for economic losses (including the reasonable expenses incurred by Grohe AG to stop the infringing acts) in the amount of RMB 100,000; 4. Dismissing the other claims of Grohe AG. Zhejiang Jianlong Sanitary Ware Co., Ltd. applied for retrial. The Supreme People's Court rendered the civil judgment (2015) Min Ti Zi No. 23 on August 11, 2015: 1. Reversing the second-instance judgment; 2. Affirming the first-instance judgment.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that the focus of the dispute in this case was whether the design of the alleged infringing product fell within the scope of protection of the design patent in question.

Article 59, Paragraph 2 of the Patent Law provides: "The scope of protection of a design patent right shall be based on the design of the product as shown in the drawings or photographs. The brief description may be used to interpret the design of the product as shown in the drawings or photographs." Article 8 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Infringement of Patent Rights (hereinafter referred to as the Interpretation on Patent Infringement Disputes) provides: "If a design identical or similar to the granted design is adopted in a product of the same or similar category as the design patent product, the people's court shall find that the alleged infringing design falls within the scope of protection of the design patent right as stipulated in Article 59, Paragraph 2 of the Patent Law." Article 10 provides: "The people's court shall judge whether designs are identical or similar based on the knowledge level and cognitive ability of ordinary consumers of the design patent product." In this case, the alleged infringing product and the design patent product in question were identical, both being shower head products. Therefore, the key issue in this case was, from the perspective of ordinary consumers, whether the design of the alleged infringing product was identical or similar to the granted design in question, specifically involving the following four issues:

I. The design features of the granted design in question

The legislative purpose of the design patent system is to protect innovative industrial designs with aesthetic appeal. For a design to obtain patent protection, it must possess identifiable innovative design that distinguishes it from prior designs. Such innovative design constitutes the design features of the granted design. Generally, designers base their designs on prior designs. For existing products, a patented design typically incorporates some elements of the prior design while also containing design elements that are neither identical nor similar to the prior design. It is these design elements that make the granted design innovative, thereby satisfying the substantive grant conditions under Article 23 of the Patent Law: not being part of the prior design and not having a conflicting application, and having obvious differences from the prior design or combinations of prior design features. The description of these design elements constitutes the design features of the granted design, reflecting its innovative content different from the prior design and the designer's creative contribution to the prior design. Because of the existence of design features, ordinary consumers can easily distinguish the granted design from the prior design; therefore, they have a significant impact on the overall visual effect of the design product. If the alleged infringing design does not include all the design features that distinguish the granted design from the prior design, it can generally be presumed that the alleged infringing design is not similar to the granted design.

Regarding the determination of design features, generally, the patentee may record design features in the brief description or may make corresponding statements regarding design features in the patent grant and invalidation procedures or infringement procedures. According to the rule of evidence that "he who asserts must prove," the patentee shall provide evidence for the design features it claims. In addition, the purpose of the patent grant and invalidation procedures is to examine whether a design meets patentability requirements; therefore, relevant records in the examination documents during such procedures have important reference significance for determining design features. Ideally, the grant and invalidation of a design patent should be based on a determination of its patentability after searching the entire prior art and selecting a comparison design. However, due to limitations in search databases and the search capabilities of invalidation requesters, the design features determined from the examination documents in the grant and invalidation procedures may not be derived from a search encompassing the entire prior art. Therefore, whether for design features proven by the patentee or determined from records in the grant and invalidation examination documents, if a third party raises an objection, the third party should be allowed to provide rebuttal evidence to overturn them. On the basis of hearing the cross-examination opinions of all parties, the people's court shall fully review the evidence and determine the design features of the granted design in accordance with the law.

In this case, the patentee Grohe claimed that the racetrack-shaped water outlet surface was a design feature of the granted design in question, which Jianlong disputed. In response, the effective judgment of the court held that, first, the granted design in question had no brief description recording its design features. During the second-instance proceedings, Grohe submitted 12 design patent documents for shower head products, 7 of which had an announcement date earlier than the filing date of the patent in question. The designs shown in the accompanying drawings did not feature a racetrack-shaped water outlet surface. In the invalidation declaration review procedure for the granted design in question, the Patent Reexamination Board issued Decision No. 17086, finding that compared to the closest comparison design, Evidence 1, the granted design in question had relatively large differences in overall shape, the transitional surfaces of the shower head and its parts, the design of the water outlet area on the front of the shower head, and the ratio of the shower head width to the handle diameter. The decision determined that these differences were design content that ordinary consumers would easily notice. Thus, the decision recognized the design of the water outlet surface shape of the shower head as one of the design features of the granted design in question. Second, although Jianlong did not recognize the racetrack-shaped water outlet surface as a design feature of the granted design in question, it did not submit any evidence during the first and second instances to prove that the racetrack-shaped water outlet surface was prior art. During the retrial review stage, Jianlong submitted the design patent view for the shower head with patent number 200630113512.5 to attempt to prove that the racetrack-shaped water outlet surface had been disclosed in prior art. Upon review, the announcement date of this design patent was earlier than the filing date of the granted design in question, so it could serve as prior art for the granted design in question. However, the front view and the reference view showing the state of use displayed that the ends of the water outlet surface were rectangular, not rounded, and the water outlet surface was not racetrack-shaped. Therefore, this court does not support Jianlong's retrial application reason regarding the claim that the racetrack-shaped water outlet surface was not a design feature of the granted design in question.

II. The parts of the product of the granted design in question that are easily directly observable during normal use

Determining the parts of the product of the granted design that are easily directly observable during normal use should be based on the perspective of ordinary consumers, considering the product's intended use and comprehensively considering the various states of use of the product. In this case, first, the granted design in question is a design for a shower head product, which consists of a shower head and a handle, with the two occupying relatively similar proportions of space in the overall product structure. The shower head product can be held by hand or mounted on a wall for use. In its normal use state, for ordinary consumers, the shower head, the handle, and the connection between them are all parts that are easily directly observable. Second, Decision No. 17086 recognized that Design Evidence 2, which had an earlier filing date, adopted the same racetrack-shaped water outlet surface as the granted design in question. However, based on the fact that "the shower head and handle of the granted design in question form a single body, the shower head and the surfaces connecting it to the handle are all curved, and the shower head tilts forward, which constitutes a large difference from the earlier filed design. These differences are all design content that ordinary consumers would easily notice," the decision found that the two were different and dissimilar designs. It can be seen that the parts of the shower head product that are easily directly observable are not limited to the water outlet surface of the shower head head. When making a comprehensive judgment on the overall visual effect of the shower head product design, the shower head, the handle, and the connection between them should all be considered as parts that are easily directly observable.

III. Whether the push button on the handle of the granted design in question is a functional design feature

Functional design features of a design patent refer to those features that, in the view of the average consumer of the design product, are solely determined by the specific function to be achieved by the product, without consideration of aesthetic factors. Normally, when designing a product appearance, designers consider both functional and aesthetic factors. On the premise of realizing the product's function, the product's appearance is improved in accordance with humanistic laws and principles, meaning the product must first achieve its function, and second, be visually aesthetic. Specifically, for a particular feature of a design, in most cases it has both functionality and ornamentality. The designer will select from among multiple designs capable of achieving a specific function the one he or she considers most aesthetically pleasing. Designs solely determined by a specific function only exist in rare special circumstances. Therefore, functional design features of a design patent include two types: first, the unique design for achieving a specific function; second, one of multiple designs for achieving a specific function, but that design is determined solely by the specific function to be achieved without regard to aesthetic considerations. The identification of a functional design feature does not depend on whether the design lacks alternatives due to functional or technical constraints, but on whether, from the perspective of the average consumer of the design product, the design is determined solely by the specific function, without needing to consider whether the design is aesthetically pleasing. Generally speaking, functional design features do not have a significant impact on the overall visual effect of a design; whereas design features that are both functional and ornamental have an impact on the overall visual effect depending on the strength of their ornamentality. The stronger the ornamentality, the relatively greater the impact on the overall visual effect; conversely, the weaker, the relatively smaller the impact.

In this case, one of the differences between the design of the patent in question and the design of the accused infringing product is that the latter lacks a track-like push button design located on the handle of the former. The function of the push button is to control the water flow switch. Whether to set a push button component is determined by whether there is a need to realize the function of controlling the water flow switch on a shower nozzle product. However, as long as a push button is set on the handle of the shower nozzle, the shape of that push button can have multiple designs. When an average consumer sees the push button on the shower nozzle handle, they will naturally pay attention to its ornamentality and consider whether the push button design is aesthetically pleasing, rather than merely considering whether the push button can realize the function of controlling the water flow switch. The designer of the design of the patent in question chose to design the push button on the handle as track-like, with the purpose of coordinating with its track-like water outlet surface and increasing the overall aesthetic appeal of the product. Therefore, the judgment at second instance that the push button in the design of the patent in question was a functional design feature was an error in the application of law, which this court hereby corrects.

IV. Whether the design of the accused infringing product and the design of the patent in question are identical or similar

Article 11 of the Interpretation on Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Disputes over Infringement of Patent Rights provides that when determining whether a design is identical or similar, a comprehensive judgment shall be made based on the design features of the patented design and the accused infringing design, taking into consideration the overall visual effect; design features primarily determined by technical functions shall not be considered. Parts that are easily directly observable during normal use of the product, as compared to other parts, and design features of the patented design that distinguish it from prior art designs, as compared to other design features of the patented design, generally have a greater impact on the overall visual effect.

In this case, compared with the design of the patent in question, the design of the accused infringing product has water outlet holes distributed within a track-shaped area on the front of the nozzle. Although there are slight differences in the number of water outlet holes and their distribution at the two ends of the water outlet surface compared with the design of the patent in question, overall, the accused infringing product adopts a track-shaped water outlet surface design that is highly similar to that of the design of the patent in question. Regarding the distinguishing design features between the two, the first instance court summarized eight aspects, which both parties did not dispute. For these distinguishing design features, first, as mentioned above, Decision No. 17086 determined that the design of the patent in question has three design features: first, the shape of the nozzle and the transition of its various surfaces; second, the shape of the water outlet surface of the nozzle; and third, the ratio of the width of the nozzle to the diameter of the handle. Apart from the design feature of the water outlet surface shape of the nozzle, design features such as the shape of the nozzle and the transition of its various surfaces, and the ratio of the nozzle width to handle diameter, also have a significant impact on the overall visual effect of the product. Although the accused infringing product adopts a track-shaped water outlet surface highly similar to that of the design of the patent in question, regarding the design feature of the shape of the nozzle and the transition of its various surfaces, in the design of the patent in question, the nozzle, handle, and the connections at various surfaces all have arc transitions, whereas in the design of the accused infringing product, the nozzle, handle, and the connections at various surfaces all have bevel transitions. This results in a clear difference in the overall design style between the two. Additionally, for distinguishing design features between the accused infringing product design and the design of the patent in question that are not design features per se, as long as they are sufficient to cause a clear difference in overall visual effect between the two, they should also be considered. Second, the nozzle, handle, and the connection between them of a shower nozzle product are all parts that are easily directly observable during normal use. When making a comprehensive judgment on the overall visual effect, the designs on these parts should be given key consideration. Specifically, the handle of the design of the patent in question is provided with a track-like push button, whereas the accused infringing product lacks this design. Since the push button is not a functional design feature, the presence or absence of the push button as a distinguishing design feature will have an impact on the overall visual effect of the product. The bevel angle at the connection between the nozzle and handle of the design of the patent in question is relatively small, whereas the bevel angle at the connection between the nozzle and handle of the accused infringing product is relatively large, resulting in a clear difference in the left side view. It is precisely because the design of the accused infringing product does not include all the design features of the design of the patent in question, and there are distinguishing design features such as the design of the handle and the connection between the nozzle and handle between the accused infringing product design and the design of the patent in question, that the two show clear differences in overall visual effect; they are neither identical nor similar, and the design of the accused infringing product does not fall within the scope of protection of the design patent in question. The judgment at second instance only focused on the design feature of the track-shaped water outlet surface of the design of the patent in question, but did not consider other design features of the design of the patent in question, nor the distinguishing design features between the accused infringing product design and the patent design on other parts easily directly observable during normal use of the shower nozzle product, thereby finding the two similar. This was an error in the application of law, which this court hereby corrects.

In summary, the design of the accused infringing product produced, offered for sale, and sold by Jianlong Company is neither identical nor similar to the design of the patent in question owned by Gaoyi Company, and does not fall within the scope of protection of the design patent in question. The acts of Jianlong Company in producing, offering for sale, and selling the accused infringing product do not constitute infringement of the patent right in question owned by Gaoyi Company. The judgment at second instance involved an error in the application of law, which this court corrects according to law.

(Judges who rendered the effective judgment: Zhou Xiang, Wu Rong, Song Shuhua)

Guiding Case No. 86

Tianjin Tianlong Seed Technology Co., Ltd. v. Jiangsu Xunong Seed Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of plant variety rights

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on March 6, 2017)

Keywords: civil / infringement of plant variety rights / mutual licensing

Ruling Gist

Where the two parties hold the male parent and female parent of a new plant variety respectively, and cannot reach a mutual licensing agreement, resulting in the inability to continue producing the new plant variety, harming the respective interests of both parties and also not conforming to the purpose of cooperative breeding. In order to safeguard social public interest, ensure national food security, promote the transformation and implementation of new plant varieties, and ensure the continued production of a new variety that has been widely planted, based on the determination that the male parent and female parent have substantially equal value in the production of the new plant variety, the people's court may directly issue an order that the two parties grant mutual licensing and mutually waive the corresponding license fees.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 5 of the Contract Law of the PRC

Articles 2, 6, and 39 of the Regulations on Protection of New Plant Varieties of the PRC

Basic Facts

Tianjin Tianlong Seed Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianlong Company) and Jiangsu Xunong Seed Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xunong Company) filed two separate lawsuits for infringement of plant variety rights against each other in court.

The three-line hybrid japonica rice variety 9 You 418, jointly bred by the Northern Hybrid Japonica Rice Engineering Technology Center (same institution as Liaoning Provincial Rice Research Institute, two names for one entity) and Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute, passed national crop variety approval on November 10, 2000. The 9 You 418 variety originated from female parent 9201A and male parent C418. On December 30, 2003, the Liaoning Provincial Rice Research Institute filed an application for a plant variety right for the C418 rice variety with the Ministry of Agriculture of the PRC, and obtained the grant on May 1, 2007, and licensed Tianlong Company to exclusively exploit the C418 plant variety right. On September 25, 2003, Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute filed an application for plant variety right protection for the Xu 9201A rice variety it had bred with the Ministry of Agriculture of the PRC, and obtained the grant on January 1, 2007. On January 3, 2008, Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute licensed Xunong Company to exclusively exploit the Xu 9201A plant variety right. Upon trial, it was found that the combination used by both Xunong Company and Tianlong Company to produce 9 You 418 was identical, both using male parent C418 and female parent Xu 9201A.

On November 14, 2010, upon the application of Tianlong Company, the first instance court commissioned the Hefei Testing Center of the Ministry of Agriculture to conduct a DNA identification on whether the accused infringing variety preserved by notarization by Tianlong Company had a parent-child relationship with the authorized variety C418. Testing conclusion: Using 48 rice SSR markers in the national standard GB/T20396-2006, DNA marker analysis was performed on 9 You 418 and C418. The results showed that among all tested markers, 9 You 418 completely inherited the banding pattern of C418, thus it could be determined that 9 You 418 and C418 had a parent-child relationship.

On August 5, 2010, upon the application of Xunong Company, the first instance court commissioned the Hefei Testing Center of the Ministry of Agriculture to conduct an identification on whether the accused infringing variety preserved by notarization by Xunong Company had a parent-child relationship with C418 and Xu 9201A. Testing conclusion: Using 48 rice SSR markers in the national standard GB/T20396-2006, DNA marker analysis was performed on the accused infringing variety and C418 and Xu 9201A. The results showed that among all tested markers, the accused infringing variety completely inherited the banding patterns of C418 and Xu 9201A, thus it could be determined that the accused infringing variety had a parent-child relationship with C418 and Xu 9201A.

According to the request for C418 variety right application submitted by Tianlong Company, its specification included the following: C418 is a restorer line bred by the North Hybrid Japonica Center using the internationally pioneering "indica-japonica bridge" technique for restoring ability, and using indica-japonica intermediate materials to construct an indica-japonica favorable gene group, resulting in a japonica restorer with indica-like morphology and specific affinity. C418 has good specific affinity, which is a performance of restorer lines bred through the "indica-japonica bridge" method, reflecting that the hybrid generation can better coordinate the ecological and genetic differences between the two major genomes of indica and japonica, thus better solving common obstacles in indica-japonica hybrids such as low seed setting rate, poor grain filling, temperature sensitivity, and premature senescence. C418 has comprehensive good traits of indica and japonica, and the hybrid combinations it produces generally exhibit high seed setting rates and certain cold tolerance.

According to the joint letter from Xunong Company and Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute to the Tianjin Municipal Seed Management Station, they stated that the medium japonica sterile line Xu 9201A independently bred by them passed in 1996, was named "9201A" before approval, abbreviated as "9A", and named "Xu 9201A" upon approval. Using Xu 9201A as the female parent, they successively selected and matched hybrid japonica rice combinations such as 9 You 138, 9 You 418, 9 You 24, etc. When filling out the national crop variety approval application form in 2000, the content regarding the parents continued to use the variety source 9201A × C418 from the 1995 combination. Xu 9201A applied for new variety right protection from the Ministry of Agriculture in July 2003, and in the variety description of the variety right application request form, it was noted that Xu 9201A had been used to breed hybrid combinations such as 9 You 138, 9 You 418, 9 You 24, 9 You 686, 9 You 88, etc. Xu 9201A and 9201A are the same medium japonica sterile line. Tianlong Company's infringing use of 9201A constitutes infringing use of Xu 9201A.

Judgment

Regarding the case filed by Tianlong Company against Xunong Company, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court rendered a civil judgment on August 31, 2011, (2009) Ning Min San Chu Zi No. 63: 1. Xunong Company shall immediately cease selling 9 You 418 hybrid japonica rice seeds, and without the permission of the right holder, shall not repeatedly use the plant new variety C418 seeds for producing 9 You 418 hybrid japonica rice seeds; 2. Xunong Company shall compensate Tianlong Company RMB 500,000 for economic losses within 15 days from the effective date of the judgment; 3. The other claims of Tianlong Company are rejected. The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 15,294 shall be borne by Xunong Company.

Regarding the case filed by Xunong Company against Tianlong Company, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court rendered a civil judgment on September 8, 2011, (2010) Ning Zhi Min Chu Zi No. 069: 1. Tianlong Company shall immediately cease infringing upon Xunong Company's exclusive exploitation right of the Xu 9201A plant variety right from the effective date of the judgment; 2. Tianlong Company shall compensate Xunong Company RMB 2,000,000 for economic losses within 10 days from the effective date of the judgment; 3. The other claims of Xunong Company are rejected.

Xunong Company and Tianlong Company, dissatisfied with the first instance judgments, appealed against the above two cases respectively. The Jiangsu High People's Court jointly rendered a civil judgment on December 29, 2013, (2011) Su Zhi Min Zhong Zi No. 0194, (2012) Su Zhi Min Zhong Zi No. 0055: 1. The civil judgments of the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court (2009) Ning Min San Chu Zi No. 63 and (2010) Ning Zhi Min Chu Zi No. 069 are set aside. 2. Tianjin Tianlong Seed Technology Co., Ltd. shall compensate Jiangsu Xunong Seed Technology Co., Ltd. RMB 500,000 within 15 days from the effective date of this judgment. 3. The other claims of Tianjin Tianlong Seed Technology Co., Ltd. and Jiangsu Xunong Seed Technology Co., Ltd. are rejected.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that: In normal circumstances, a plant variety right, as an important intellectual property right, should be respected and protected. Article 6 of the Regulations on Protection of New Plant Varieties clearly stipulates: "The unit or individual that has completed the breeding shall have the exclusive right to its authorized variety. No unit or individual may, without the permission of the variety rights owner, produce or sell the propagating material of the authorized variety for commercial purposes, or repeatedly use the propagating material of the authorized variety for producing the propagating material of another variety for commercial purposes." However, it should be pointed out that this provision does not apply to the circumstances of this case. First, the cooperative breeding of 9 You 418 originated from the domestic hybrid rice scientific research cooperation in the 1990s, and was itself a gratuitous combination. The 9 You 418 variety has excellent traits, is widely planted in Jiangsu, Anhui, Henan, and other places, and is widely welcomed by the majority of planting farmers. It has become the leading variety of medium japonica hybrid rice. The fact that both parties accuse each other of infringement is itself sufficient to indicate that the 9 You 418 variety has high economic value and market prospects, involving significant economic interests of both the cooperative parties (Liaoning Provincial Rice Research Institute and Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute) and the parties in this case. During the second instance, the court made extensive mediation efforts, hoping that both parties could grant mutual licensing so that the excellent variety 9 You 418 could continue to be produced. Both parties also agreed to grant mutual licensing for the variety rights in question, but only because the first instance judgment ordered Tianlong Company to compensate Xunong Company RMB 2,000,000 and Xunong Company to compensate Tianlong Company RMB 500,000, and the parties could not reach a compromise on the difference of RMB 1,500,000, the mediation failed. The failure of Tianlong Company and Xunong Company to reach a compromise, resulting in the inability to continue producing the 9 You 418 variety, cannot be considered as merely affecting the interests of both parties. In fact, it has already harmed the implementation of the national food security strategy, harmed the public interest, and is inconsistent with the fundamental purpose of the original cooperative breeding between Liaoning Provincial Rice Research Institute and Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute, and also does not meet the fundamental requirement of promoting the transformation and implementation of new plant varieties. On the surface, the acts of both parties are aimed at protecting their respective intellectual property rights, but the actual result is to harm the utilization of intellectual property rights and the transformation of scientific and technological achievements. Given that these two cases have already involved public interests such as national food production security, affecting the promotion of the excellent variety 9 You 418, both parties' exercise of the exclusive exploitation license rights of the plant variety rights in question should be restricted, i.e., when producing the 9 You 418 rice variety, each party should allow the other to use its own parent propagating materials. This result is obviously beneficial to the common interests of the cooperative parties (Liaoning Provincial Rice Research Institute and Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute) and the parties in this case, and also beneficial to the interests of the majority of planting farmers. Therefore, the first instance judgment ordering the parties in these two cases to cease infringement and compensate each other for losses was improper and should be corrected. Second, 9 You 418 is a three-line hybrid combination, integrating the excellent traits of both parents with significant heterosis. The female parent sterile line plays an important role, and the breeding of male parent C418 also successfully solved the major problem of three-line hybrid japonica rice matching. In the 9 You 418 combination, the male parent and female parent have equal status and function. The court ruled that the cooperative parties of the 9 You 418 rice variety, Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute and Liaoning Provincial Rice Research Institute, and their present parties Xunong Company and Tianlong Company, each have the right to use the other's authorized parent propagating materials, and shall mutually waive license fees, but only for the purpose of producing and selling the 9 You 418 rice variety, and not for other commercial purposes. Because Xunong Company made many commercial efforts and conducted planting technology research to promote the 9 You 418 variety, while Tianlong Company entered the production field after the 9 You 418 variety had gained widespread market recognition, thus significantly reducing its market cost for promoting the variety. To reflect fairness and reasonableness, the court also ordered Tianlong Company to pay Xunong Company RMB 500,000 as economic compensation. Finally, given that both parties produce 9 You 418 separately, there is indeed some market competition and conflict of interest. The court advised both parties to comply with the relevant provisions of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the PRC, operate in good faith, compete orderly, ensure quality, and especially clearly mark their respective commercial identifiers to prevent new disputes and conflicts, jointly maintaining the good reputation of the 9 You 418 variety.

(Judges who rendered the effective judgment: Song Jian, Gu Tao, Yuan Tao)

Guiding Case No. 87

Guo Mingsheng, Guo Mingfeng, Sun Shubiao — crime of counterfeiting registered trademark

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on March 6, 2017)

Keywords: criminal / crime of counterfeiting a registered trademark / illegal business volume / online sales / reputation manipulation (credit-swindling)

Ruling Gist

The amounts of illegal business volume and illegal gains in the crime of counterfeiting a registered trademark shall be determined by comprehensively considering evidence such as the defendants' confessions, witness testimony, victims' statements, electronic data from online sales, records of the defendants' bank account transactions, delivery notes, computer system records of the express company, and accounting records kept by the defendants. If the defendant argues that the online sales records contain fabricated transactions to boost credibility but fails to provide evidence to support this assertion, the defense shall not be accepted.

Relevant Legal Provision

Article 213 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The prosecutorial authority alleged that during the period from late November 2013 to June 2014, the defendant Guo Mingsheng, for the purpose of seeking illegal benefits, in collusion with the defendants Sun Shubiao and Guo Mingfeng, without authorization from Samsung (China) Investment Co., Ltd., purchased counterfeit Samsung mobile phone bare handsets and accessories from others for assembly, used the online store "Samsung Digital Counter" that he had opened on Taobao.com to advertise as "genuine products," and openly sold them to the public at prices significantly lower than the market price. A total of over 20,000 counterfeit Samsung mobile phones were sold, with a sales amount of over RMB 20 million and illegal gains of over RMB 2 million. The defendants should be held criminally liable for the crime of counterfeiting a registered trademark. Defendant Guo Mingsheng played a principal role in the joint crime and was the principal offender. Defendants Guo Mingfeng and Sun Shubiao played a secondary role in the joint crime and were accomplices, and should be given a lighter punishment.

The defendants Guo Mingsheng, Sun Shubiao, and Guo Mingfeng and their defense counsel did not dispute the criminal facts that they assembled counterfeit Samsung mobile phones and sold them through the Taobao online store without authorization from the registrant of the "SΛMSUNG" trademark. However, they raised objections to the amounts of illegal business volume and illegal gains, arguing that their Taobao online store had engaged in reputation manipulation (credit-swindling) by hiring others, and that the actual transaction volume was only over 10,000 units.

The court found through trial that "SΛMSUNG" is a trademark registered in China by Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd., with a validity period until July 27, 2021. Samsung (China) Investment Co., Ltd. is a company invested in and established in China by Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd., and specifically authorized by Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. to manage and handle legal matters regarding intellectual property rights, including trademarks, patents, and copyrights owned by Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. In November 2013, defendant Guo Mingsheng purchased a Taobao store with the shop owner "Wang Liang" and account name "play2011-1985" through an online intermediary, renamed it "Samsung Digital Counter," and without authorization from Samsung (China) Investment Co., Ltd., purchased counterfeit Samsung I8552 mobile phone bare handsets and accessories from Shenzhen Huaqiangbei Yuanwang Digital City and Shenzhen Futian District Tongtiandi Mobile Phone Market for assembly, and advertised and sold them as "genuine products" through "Samsung Digital Counter" on Taobao.com. Defendant Guo Mingfeng was responsible for the customer service work of the online store and the management of customer service staff. Defendant Sun Shubiao was responsible for the purchase, packaging of the counterfeit Samsung I8552 mobile phone bare handsets and accessories, and contacting the express company for delivery. Up to June 2014, the online store assembled and sold over 20,000 counterfeit Samsung I8552 mobile phones, with an illegal business volume of over RMB 20 million and illegal gains of over RMB 2 million.

Judgment

The Suqian Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province rendered a criminal judgment on September 8, 2015, in the case (2015) Suzhong Zhixing Chu Zi No. 0004, sentencing defendant Guo Mingsheng for the crime of counterfeiting a registered trademark to five years of fixed-term imprisonment and a fine of RMB 1.6 million; sentencing defendant Sun Shubiao for the crime of counterfeiting a registered trademark to three years of fixed-term imprisonment, suspended for five years, and a fine of RMB 200,000; and sentencing defendant Guo Mingfeng for the crime of counterfeiting a registered trademark to three years of fixed-term imprisonment, suspended for four years, and a fine of RMB 200,000. After the judgment was pronounced, none of the three defendants appealed, and the judgment has become effective.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that the defendants Guo Mingsheng, Guo Mingfeng, and Sun Shubiao, without authorization from the registrant of the "SΛMSUNG" trademark, purchased mobile phone headsets and accessories bearing the counterfeit "SΛMSUNG" registered trademark, assembled them into mobile phones bearing the counterfeit "SΛMSUNG" registered trademark, and sold them through the online store as "genuine products." This conduct constituted the act of using a trademark identical to the registered trademark on the same goods without permission of the owner of the registered trademark. The illegal business volume amounted to over RMB 20 million, and the illegal gains amounted to over RMB 2 million. The circumstances were particularly serious, and their conduct constituted the crime of counterfeiting a registered trademark. Although the defendants Guo Mingsheng, Guo Mingfeng, and Sun Shubiao argued that their online store sales records included instances of reputation manipulation (credit-swindling) and raised objections to the amounts of illegal business volume and illegal gains alleged by the prosecutorial authority, the multiple confessions made by the three defendants to the public security organs, as well as the delivery notes seized by the public security organs, the payment records from Alipay to defendant Guo Mingfeng's bank account, the outward payment records from Guo Mingfeng's bank account, the Taobao records of "Samsung Digital Counter," the computer system records of the express company, and the notes seized on site by the public security organs, all corroborated each other. By comprehensively considering the evidence provided by the prosecutorial authority, it could be established that the prosecutorial authority's allegation that the three defendants sold a total of over 20,000 counterfeit Samsung I8552 mobile phones, with a sales amount of over RMB 20 million and illegal gains of over RMB 2 million, was valid. The defendants' defense that the sales records included acts of reputation manipulation (credit-swindling) was unsupported by evidence and was not accepted. The defendants Guo Mingsheng, Guo Mingfeng, and Sun Shubiao were joint offenders. Defendant Guo Mingsheng played a principal role and was the principal offender. Defendants Guo Mingfeng and Sun Shubiao played a secondary role in the joint crime and were accomplices, and could be given a lighter punishment according to law. Therefore, the above judgment was rendered according to law.

(Judges who rendered the effective judgment: Cheng Liming, Zhu Geng, Bai Jin)
